text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
- The message from Denver -- prosperity and peace in a global partnership. Russia's position honoured. Warnings sent to Bosnia. Environmental protection issue controversial.

- CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble opposed to "decimal discussion" on whether Germany will qualify for EMU. He also warns Germany against being "arrogant" towards other EU nations en route to single European currency.

- German industry raises storm of protest against tax reform plans. Federal Chamber of Industry (BDI) president Hans Oalf Henkel calls coalition's tax reform proposals unacceptable. Will cause massive burdens to industry.
- Finance Minster Theo Waigel wants to get into the wallets of German farmers. To close budget holes, Waigel considering cutting 615 million marks in subsidies to farmers.
- German industry incensed at Bonn's tax reform plans. Leading industrialists heap scorn on government's plans to reduce tax loopholes.

- Schleswig-Holstein premier Heide Simonis calls for more pressure to be applied on welfare recipients who turn down job offers. She urges that welfare payments be reduced if no reasonable reason for turning job offer down.
- Hefty dispute over environmental protectionat G7 summit in Denver. United States opposed to proposal from EU nations to cut greenhouse gas output to 15 percent below 1990 levels by year 2010.

- Bonn's partners demand faster reforms. Leaders at G7 meeting in Denver point to high unemployment in Germany, France and Italy. Russia an equal partner of G8. No agreement on binding environmental protection targets
- First shareholder meeting for Deutsche Telekom this week in Frankfurt after one of the largest flotations in European history last year.
- 1996 was good year for German car makers Mercedes, BMW and Audi. VW raised profits but its return on investment still low. Opel's profits declined and Ford fell sharply into the red.

- G7 meeting calls upon Bonn to move forward with reform. Tension at meeting of the eight. Criticism of United States for trying to push U.S. model on other states. Chancellor Helmut Kohl fails with his environmental protection push.
